# Combobox

<!-- Generated by `pnpm readme:build`. Edit only inside the hand-written block. -->

forms · tier 2 · beta · runs in the browser.

<!-- hand-written -->

## When to use

For one choice out of a list a person types into, from a few options to thousands. For a short list
with nothing to type, a Select. It is one element that takes its options as data.

```tsx
import { Combobox } from 'topclassui/combobox'
```

```tsx
<label htmlFor="framework">Framework</label>
<Combobox id="framework" name="framework" items={[{ value: 'next', label: 'Next.js' }, { value: 'astro', label: 'Astro' }]} defaultValue="next" />
```

**A name is required.** `id` for a `<label htmlFor>` (the root hands it to the input), or
`aria-label`, or `aria-labelledby`; the type refuses a Combobox with none. While the list is open
Base UI hides everything else from assistive technology, the label too, and Chrome then gives the
input no name; so while the list is open the input carries the label's text as `aria-label`, read at
each open and dropped at each close, when the label names it again. Pass `aria-label` or
`aria-labelledby` yourself and nothing is copied.

**`items` is plain data**, `{ value, label, disabled? }`, so a server page renders a Combobox with
no function crossing to the browser. `value` is what the form receives, unique in its list; `label`
is what the row and the input show and what typing is matched against. The input prints the label
of the value in the server HTML. An option whose `value` is `''` is a value like any other. Keep
`items` the same array between renders, or the options are rebuilt each time.

**A Field's props spread onto it**, as they do onto an Input:

```tsx
export function FrameworkField(control: { id: string, name: string, required: boolean, 'aria-describedby': string, 'aria-invalid': boolean }) {
  return <Combobox {...control} items={[{ value: 'next', label: 'Next.js' }]} />
}
```

**The state.** `value` and `defaultValue` are a string, or `null` for nothing chosen;
`onValueChange` gets the same and Base UI's details. Your handler runs first, so `details.cancel()`
keeps the value. What is typed is Base UI's `inputValue`, `defaultInputValue` and
`onInputValueChange`.

**The form.** With a `name`, a hidden input sends `name=<value>`, and `name=` with nothing chosen,
also when text was typed and nothing picked. Before the page hydrates it sends the default; text
typed into the input then is not sent, and hydration puts the label of the default back. **A form
reset**, a reset button or a React 19 form action that settles brings it back to the `defaultValue`
of the latest render, on screen and in the form; a controlled Combobox keeps its owner's value. A
reset calls no `onValueChange`. **`required`** with nothing chosen blocks a submit. Before the page
hydrates the browser then sends the focus to the hidden input, a box of 1 px; after it, to the input.

**The keyboard**, the editable combobox of the Authoring Practices. The input keeps the focus; the
highlight moves by `aria-activedescendant`. A press or ArrowDown opens the list on its first row;
typing filters it ("contains", in any case). ArrowDown and ArrowUp move and wrap through the input:
ArrowUp past the first row goes back to the input, once more to the last row. Enter chooses and
closes; Escape closes. **Escape on the closed input clears the value**, so the form sends `name=`:
that is Base UI's. ArrowLeft, ArrowRight, Home and End move the caret in the text, in Arabic too.

**The list** is seven rows tall (`--tc-list-rows`), or `visibleRows` (1 to 20), and scrolls inside
itself; the page behind does not move. A row is 40 px, 44 px under a finger, one line that ends in
an ellipsis. It is as wide as the input. **It is windowed** above 200 options (`virtualize`, `'auto'`
by default; `true` always, `false` never): only the rows in view and a few around them are mounted,
about twenty, and the highlight still reaches every option, a row that was never mounted included.
A query with no match says `emptyFallback`, or `collection.noResults` from the provider's labels.

**Pages.** The component asks and never fetches (R-8.5-2). With `hasMore`, it calls `loadMore()`
once per length of `items` when the open list comes within `loadMoreThreshold` rows (10; 0 to 200)
of its end, and never while it is closed; you append the next page to `items`. `status` says what
is on its way: `'loading'` draws a spinner in place of the caret, marks the input `aria-busy` and,
with no options yet, says `common.loading` in the list; `'loading-more'` says `state.loadingMore`
under the options. Filtering runs over the options loaded so far.

**The width** belongs to a box around the input: the width of an Input of the same `size`, and less
when the parent is narrower. `fullWidth` fills the parent. A width class in `className` lands on the
input inside the box: use `fullWidth` and size the parent.

**`placement`** takes the twelve shared values, `bottom-start` by default; `start` and `end` are
the reading sides. The list opens 6 px off the input, flips at an edge and stays 8 px inside the
screen.

**`modal`** is Base UI's, `false` by default: the page scrolls and takes presses while the list is
open. `true` locks the page while it is open.

**In a Dialog.** The list paints above it. The first Escape closes the list; the second, on the
closed input that holds a value, clears the value and leaves the Dialog open; the third closes the
Dialog. So a person who presses Escape to leave the Dialog loses the chosen value first: Base UI's.

**`invalid`** sets `aria-invalid` on the input: its line turns red and thickens. **`disabled`** is
the real attribute, so the form sends nothing. **`readOnly`** keeps the value in the form and takes
the soft fill. **`maxLength`** caps the typed query at 256 by default; `null` removes the cap; no
counter is drawn.

**Arabic.** The caret and the tick sit at the left, and `bottom-start` lines the list up with the
right edge of the input. The list takes its direction and language from the nearest
`TopClassProvider`, also in an island; with none, those of the page.

**On the element.** `className`, `style`, `ref`, `aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid` and the rest go
to the input, an `<input role="combobox">`. The box around it takes nothing from you.

**Known gaps.** While it is open Base UI renders two hidden buttons named "Dismiss" in English, and
no prop replaces the name (R-5.11-1). The README generator prints `unknown` for `virtualize`
(`'auto' | boolean`) and for `maxLength` (`number | null`).

### What Base UI gives

| Base UI | Here |
|---|---|
| `Combobox.Root`, `Input`, `Portal`, `Positioner`, `Popup`, `List`, `Item`, `ItemIndicator`, `Empty`, `Status`, `useFilteredItems`, `createItems` | one `Combobox` |
| `value`, `defaultValue`, `onValueChange` with `details.cancel()` | the same names, a string or `null`; the value is held for the form reset |
| `items`, any shape | `{ value, label, disabled? }` only, made a collection with `createItems` |
| `virtualized` | always set: the list is windowed by the shared `useCollection` |
| `name`, `form`, `id`, `required`, `disabled`, `readOnly`, `inputRef`, `autoComplete`, `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange`, `onOpenChangeComplete`, `inputValue`, `defaultInputValue`, `onInputValueChange`, `filter`, `autoHighlight`, `highlightItemOnHover`, `loopFocus`, `openOnInputClick`, `onItemHighlighted`, `actionsRef`, `modal`, `locale` | passed through |
| `multiple`, `filteredItems`, `grid`, `inline`, `limit`, `itemToStringLabel`, `itemToStringValue`, `isItemEqualToValue` | not props |

### Not built

The parts as exports, `multiple` and chips, groups, a clear button and a trigger button (the caret
is decoration: a press on the input opens it), the magnifier at the start (choice 25), an error row
with a retry, `Autocomplete`, async search helpers, a Drawer on a phone, a counter on the input,
`selectedItem` (a value whose option is in no loaded page shows an empty input), a stale `loadMore`
dropped by request id, a skeleton (use `InputSkeleton`).

## Import

```tsx
import { Combobox } from 'topclassui/combobox'
```

## Props

Required: `items`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` or `id`. Every other prop below is optional.

| Prop | Required | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `items` | **yes** | `readonly ListOption[]` | - | The options, as plain data a Server Component can pass. Keep the array stable between renders. |
| `aria-label` | **yes**, or `aria-labelledby` or `id` | `string` | - | The name read out when no visible label names the control. |
| `aria-labelledby` | **yes**, or `aria-label` or `id` | `string` | - | The id of the visible text that names the control. |
| `id` | **yes**, or `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` | `string` | - | The id a `<label htmlFor>` points at. |
| `className` | no | `string` | - | On the input, merged last. |
| `container` | no | `Base.Portal.Props['container']` | - | Where the list mounts; the body when left out. |
| `defaultValue` | no | `string \| null` | - | The value the page opens on, and the one a form reset returns to. |
| `emptyFallback` | no | `ReactNode` | - | What an empty list says, in place of labels.collection.noResults. |
| `fullWidth` | no | `boolean` | `false` | Fills its parent instead of taking the width of an Input. |
| `hasMore` | no | `boolean` | `false` | More pages exist, so loadMore is called when the open list nears its end. |
| `invalid` | no | `boolean` | `false` | Marks the value as wrong: sets aria-invalid on the input, whose line turns to danger and thickens. |
| `keepMounted` | no | `Base.Portal.Props['keepMounted']` | - | Keeps the list mounted while it is closed. |
| `loadMore` | no | `(() => void \| Promise<void>)` | - | Called with no argument when the list nears its end while hasMore is set, never while closed. Client-only, or a Server Action. |
| `loadMoreThreshold` | no | `integer`, min 0, max 200 | `10` | How many rows from the end loadMore is called, clamped. |
| `maxLength` | no | `unknown` | `256` | The cap on the typed query, 256 by default; null removes it. No counter is drawn. |
| `onValueChange` | no | `((value: string \| null, details: ComboboxChan...` | - | Called with the value of the chosen option, or null when the choice is cleared. Client-only. |
| `placement` | no | `top` \| `top-start` \| `top-end` \| `bottom` \| `bottom-start` \| `bottom-end` \| `start` \| `start-top` \| `start-bottom` \| `end` \| `end-top` \| `end-bottom` | `"bottom-start"` | The side and alignment the list opens at; start and end mirror in Arabic. |
| `ref` | no | `Ref<HTMLInputElement>` | - | The visible input. |
| `size` | no | `xs` \| `sm` \| `md` \| `lg` \| `xl` \| `custom` | `"md"` | The height, padding and type step of the input; custom emits no size classes. |
| `status` | no | `idle` \| `loading` \| `loading-more` | `"idle"` | loading draws a spinner and, with no options, says so; loading-more says so under the list. |
| `value` | no | `string \| null` | - | The chosen option's value, or null for none. Use with onValueChange when controlled. |
| `virtualize` | no | `unknown` | `"auto"` | auto windows the list above 200 options; true always, false never. |
| `visibleRows` | no | `integer`, min 1, max 20 | `7` | Rows the list shows before it scrolls, clamped. Left out, the --tc-list-rows knob applies. |

Anything else is passed to the root element, so standard attributes (`onClick`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, `id`) work. `className` is merged last, so yours wins a conflict, and `ref` is a normal prop.
